items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

Boston Blue ‘s newest episode took an emotional turn when a main character revealed a past suicide attempt.

During the Friday, November 13, episode of the CBS series, Sean Reagan ( Mika Amonsen ) and Jonah Silver ( Marcus Scribner ) searched for a fellow officer, whom they believed was a risk to himself. They were able to talk him down after Sean revealed his own mental health challenges. He specifically recalled struggling with suicidal ideation after his mother’s death and how a past attempt had pushed him to address his issues.

Before Boston Blue , Sean’s journey was featured on Blue Bloods , which ran from 2010 to 2024. The spinoff, which premiered in October 2025, kicked off with Danny ( Donnie Wahlberg ) visiting Boston after Sean ended up in a coma. This version of Sean looked a little different, as Andrew Terraciano previously played the role.

“There’s been some negativity [from viewers], for sure,” Amonsen exclusively told Us in November 2025 about taking over the part. “But when I look under those posts that have the negativity, there’s a lot of fans rallying for Sean and people saying that they really enjoyed this character that I’ve created — or my version of character.”

Mika Amonsen Breaks Silence on 'Boston Blue' Recasting Andrew Terraciano 

Amonsen noted that he wanted to make Blue Bloods fans happy with his performance, saying, “They’re really enjoying the show, and they love where it’s going in terms of Sean, and that makes me happy.”

The actor recalled feeling “ a ton of pressure ” over the situation.

items.title: Golden Bachelorette's Joan Vassos Reveals Why She and Chock Chapple Split
items.summary:
Joan Vassos is sharing candid details about why she and Chock Chapple called off their engagement.

The Golden Bachelorette star, 63, reflected on the breakup in an interview with People on Friday, November 13, explaining why the couple ultimately weren’t meant to be.

Vasso told the outlet that she had hoped their relationship would lead to marriage but things didn’t quite work out as planned.

“When Chock got down on one knee, I was like, ‘I think I can do this. I’m ready to make this leap of faith. I actually have enough faith in this relationship to think that it might really succeed, that we might really get married,’” Vassos recalled.

Golden Bachelorette's Joan Vassos and Chock Chapple Split After 2 Years 

The reality star added that she had also prepared herself for the possibility that their romance might not last, telling herself, “If it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out.”

Over the course of their two-year engagement , Vassos and Chapple, also 63, shared plenty of major milestones, from introducing each other to their families and taking vacations together to navigating some difficult moments.

“We did a lot,” Vassos told the outlet. “I had two sons get married, three grandbabies born. I mean, a lot happened in our two years of engagement. We did all the things.”

The pair also supported each other through Chapple’s recent medical challenges. In August, he revealed that he had undergone surgery to have his prostate removed following a cancer scare.

items.title: 'Life With Derek' Stepsiblings Leaned Into 'Undeniable Chemistry' Onscreen
items.summary:
Life With Derek ’s Michael Seater has always been well aware of fan chatter about the dynamic he shared with his onscreen stepsister.

During a recent appearance on the “Back to the Best” podcast , Seater, 39, confessed that he and costar, Ashley Leggat , 40, purposely leaned in to their “undeniable chemistry” despite playing family members.

“Here’s the thing, we had an undeniable chemistry that fans loved,” Seater noted.

Life With Derek was a Canadian TV show broadcast via Disney Channel in the United States from 2005 to 2009. Leggat starred as Casey McDonald while Seater played the role of Derek Venturi. In the show, Casey’s mom married Derek’s dad, making them stepsiblings. However, viewers were convinced there was an underlying sexual tension between the two.

Does Robbie Amell Think 'Life With Derek' Was About Stepsiblings in Love? 

“Listen, romance has never been bigger, right?” Seater said, before joking that fans seemingly would have loved Derek and Casey to follow some sort of enemies-to-lovers trope.

“So fans want that and they’re like, well they’re stepsiblings so technically…” he quipped.

Seater said he and Leggat knew how fans perceived their dynamic at the time that the show was being made.

Life With Derek cast. (Photo by Disney Channel/ Everett Collection) 
 “In these early days of the internet, our producers don’t know that there’s like forums online where people are talking, but we do,” Seater recalled. “We saw that the fans were talking about it. And so, and I can say this because I’ve said it a million times, we knew that the fans liked it, so we…

“I got the offer and I asked first, ‘Does a holiday movie — is there a kiss?’ And they’re like, ‘Yeah, there’s a kiss at the end,’” he recalled. “I’m like, ‘Alright, let me talk to Kelsey.’”

Joey Graziadei Admits to Struggles in Kelsey Relationship After 'Bachelor' 

Anderson, however, was totally unfazed by the idea of him kissing another woman after the couple met on The Bachelor in 2023, getting engaged during the season 28 finale, which aired in 2024 .

“Kelsey, like, literally laughed in my face,” Anderson remembered. “She’s like, ‘I saw you kiss all these girls on TV. This is literally the foundation of our relationship. If you think I’m going to keep you from getting your first acting opportunity, because there’s a kiss scene, you’re crazy.’”

Graziadei said he was just making sure she was cool with the idea, telling her, “I was like, ‘I’m trying to be a good fiancé.’ I’m asking.”

items.title: Phil Collins Considers Touring Again After Years of Health Problems
items.summary:
Phil Collins has not given up on the possibility of touring again despite spending the better part of 20 years battling numerous health problems .

“Never say never … I do think, every now and again, that I’m not finished [touring],” Collins, 75, revealed in a recent interview with the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame . “On the other hand, I think of the practicalities.”

Those everyday “practicalities” would include giving up his current lifestyle for the grueling physical toll of life on the road.

“I’ll enjoy the sunshine, you know, just there’s no sweat, don’t have to do anything. Just get up and say, ‘What am I going to do today?'” he said. “But on the other hand, once you’ve been on stage all your life and tasted that, it’s difficult to stop.”

Phil Collins Hospitalized for Surgery: Report 

As for the possibility of releasing new music, Collins teased, “I’ve got ideas. I got things I finished. I’ve got things that I’ve half finished.”

Collins has struggled with various health issues, including type 2 diabetes, for many years. In February 2025, he told Mojo that he was no longer “hungry” to keep playing music because he’d been “very sick.”

The rocker suffered a serious spinal injury in 2007 that caused nerve damage. While the injury initially left him completely incapable of playing drums, he underwent corrective surgery in 2015.

Collins recovered well enough to reunite with Genesis bandmates Tony Banks and Mike Rutherford for the group’s The Last Domino? Tour in 2021, though his physical limitations mandated that Collins perform from a chair.

items.t: Phil Collins Considers Touring Again After Years of Health Problems

Always wondered how celebrities do Christmas, what they wear, eat, and always buy ready-made? The chef and campaigner talks whisky, matching waistcoats and the joy of a local bookshop with the Filter

• Don’t get the Filter delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Jamie Oliver is a global chef and campaigner with a 27-year television and publishing career. He is working to improve people’s relationship with food and, through his Ministry of Food, aims to teach more than 1 million people to cook by 2030. Jamie lives in Essex with his wife, Jools, and their children. His latest book, 20 Minute Meals: Real Fast Food, is published by Penguin.

items.title: One leg in the air like you just don’t care? Eight classic power poses – and what they really mean
items.summary:
The pose of the moment is eye-catching and a little alarming. But it’s not the first to cause a stir. Here is a history of such stances, from the Angelina Jolie leg flash to Andrew Scott’s insouciant hand-in-pocket

You think you know your culture back to front, all the snooker moves that drove us to this point, and then something happens and you realise you haven’t been paying attention. I’m thinking of the modern celebrity power pose: one leg shooting high in the air, preferably while wearing a ballgown. It has to be a woman. If a man did it, he would be mocking a woman, making his power message: “I’m brave enough, and comfortable enough in my own skin, to mock ladies.” Which is powerful, to be fair.

When women do it – Victoria Beckham started it, Myleene Klass has dabbled, Amanda Holden does it all the time (even standing up) – other women liken them to a cat licking, sorry, grooming its butt. Once, memorably, Taylor Swift posted her cat doing this very thing on Insta. But what is this pose meant to be saying? “I may be a pop star or a TV celebrity, but with my flexibility and muscle tone, I am ready…
